attacks.reason: The conductive mesh may not be able to maintain structural integrity in the presence of moisture or other environmental stressors.
attacks.evidence_required: Studies on the durability of copper mesh in various environmental conditions

attacks.reason: The transfer of structural integrity from the conductive mesh to the electrode gel is not clearly justified.
attacks.evidence_required: A detailed explanation of the underlying physics or a mathematical model demonstrating the transfer of structural integrity

attacks.reason: The conductive mesh may fail in the presence of high-frequency electromagnetic interference.
attacks.evidence_required: Studies on the effects of electromagnetic interference on copper mesh and silicone gel

attacks.reason: The combination of a conductive mesh and electrode gel is not an obvious solution to maintaining structural integrity.
attacks.evidence_required: A survey of existing literature on electrode gel design and a comparison with existing solutions

attacks.reason: No existing reference discloses the same nucleus of a conductive mesh embedded within electrode gel.
attacks.evidence_required: A thorough search of existing patents and literature on electrode gel design

attacks.reason: The production of a thin, conductive mesh within the electrode gel may be impractical or expensive.
attacks.evidence_required: Cost-benefit analysis and a feasibility study on the production process

attacks.reason: The expected effect of improved ECG signal quality may not be directly measurable or falsifiable.
attacks.evidence_required: A clear and measurable hypothesis on the effect of the conductive mesh on ECG signal quality

refinement_needed: A more detailed explanation of the underlying physics, a clearer justification of the transfer of structural integrity, and a more practical and measurable solution to maintaining structural integrity.
